Resolves #19843

The engine e2e tier runs as four shards instead of three, so each shard's test step is back under the five-minute ceiling. Dev's push of `e161f623bf` timed shards 1 and 3 out at 5.1 minutes with every test passed. The workflow header's rule applies: a shard nearing the ceiling gets a sibling, never a higher ceiling.

A gate job named `e2e-engine` needs the matrix and fails unless every shard succeeded. Dev's ruleset `19087298` requires the shards by name (`e2e-engine (1/3)`, `(2/3)`, `(3/3)`), and those names carry the count that adding a sibling changes. Requiring the one gate context instead means the next shard needs no ruleset edit. The ceiling, the dispatch path and the selection stay as they are.

Evidence: L3 (this PR's own hosted run is the receipt) → L3 required (AC-2 and AC-3 are measured on that run). Residual: AC-5, Residual-Owner: #19652.

agent-preflight: not hosted here; the baseline jobs run in CI.

### `@neo-opus-grace` commented on 2026-10-17T22:18:48Z

**[ADDRESSED]: the CI review hold.** Emmy, you're right, and my diff missed it. Ruleset `19087298` requires the shards by name, so `(1/4)` … `(4/4)` satisfy nothing it asks for.

I took your second option, a stable context, at `35eb58f821`. A gate job named `e2e-engine` needs the matrix, and its one step fails unless `needs.e2e-engine.result` is `success`, so a failed, cancelled or skipped shard fails it. No shard leaves the merge gate. It runs on pull requests and dev pushes, not on dispatch probes.

I chose this over requiring `(1/4)` … `(4/4)` because the shard count is the ceiling's own instrument: the header's rule changes it whenever the tier grows, and each change would need another ruleset edit.

The swap is the operator's, so I've asked him: in `19087298`, replace `e2e-engine (1/3)`, `(2/3)` and `(3/3)` with `e2e-engine`, keeping integration `15368` and every other field. Until then this head stays BLOCKED. The ticket (#19843) and the PR body carry the new AC-3 and AC-4.
